items.title: UN Rights Chief Urges Restraint in Azad Kashmir, Calls for Probe into Deaths Ahead of Elections
items.subtitle: UN Human Rights Office calls for impartial investigations, restoration of internet access and inclusive political dialogue ahead of July 27 elections.
items.excerpt: The United Nations High Commissioner for Human Rights has appealed for calm in Pakistan-administered Azad Kashmir following weeks of unrest that have reportedly left dozens dead ahead of legislative elections.
items.summary: Volker Türk, through the UN Human Rights Office, called for restraint in Pakistan-administered Azad Kashmir, urging authorities to investigate deaths linked to recent unrest, guarantee due process for detainees, restore internet access and engage in meaningful political dialogue.
items.author: The Mirror Jammu Kashmir Special Correspondent

heroImage.alt: UN Human Rights Office briefing in Geneva on unrest in Azad Kashmir
heroImage.caption: The UN Human Rights Office in Geneva calls for impartial investigations into deaths linked to unrest in Pakistan-administered Azad Kashmir and urges restoration of internet access.

body.text: GENEVA, July 17, 2026 — The United Nations High Commissioner for Human Rights has called for calm and restraint in Pakistan-administered Azad Kashmir following weeks of unrest that have reportedly left dozens of people dead ahead of legislative elections scheduled for July 27.

Speaking at a press briefing in Geneva, Jeremy Laurence, spokesperson for the Office of the United Nations High Commissioner for Human Rights (OHCHR), said Human Rights Chief Volker Türk was concerned by reports of escalating violence involving protesters and security personnel since June.
Laurence said the High Commissioner was appealing for calm across the territory and called for prompt, thorough and impartial investigations into all deaths linked to the unrest.

UN Human Rights Chief Volker Türk appeals for calm in Pakistan-administered Kashmir amid a wave of unrest ahead of regional elections at the end of the month. Dozens of people, mostly protesters but also law enforcement personnel, have reportedly been killed since June ahead of the vote for the Legislative Assembly on 27 July. We call for prompt, thorough and impartial investigations into all deaths that have occurred due to the unrest, both amongst protesters and members of security forces.
Concerns Over Ban on JAAC
The OHCHR also expressed concern over the banning of the Joint Awami Action Committee (JAAC), a movement involved in organising recent demonstrations across the territory.

The Joint Awami Action Committee, or the JAAC  a movement behind the protests comprising traders, transporters, students, lawyers, activists and others — has been banned under anti-terrorism laws for allegedly threatening public order and security. Some of the group's leaders have subsequently been arrested.

The UN Human Rights Office said the criminalisation of a civil society organisation and the imposition of restrictions on public gatherings raise concerns regarding rights protected under international human rights standards.

The criminalization of a civil society organization and imposition of strict limitations on gatherings raise serious concerns about infringements on the rights to freedom of expression, peaceful assembly and association.
The Office further stated that detained JAAC leaders should have access to legal representation and family members, while their rights to due process and fair trial must be guaranteed.
Internet Restrictions Criticised

The OHCHR also raised concerns regarding internet restrictions imposed during the unrest, stating that limitations on communications can affect the ability of people to seek, receive and share information.

Restrictions in the area on access to the Internet are also concerning, as they disproportionately restrict the enjoyment of the right to freedom of expression, including freedom to seek, receive and impart information at a time when tensions are running high. We urge the authorities to ensure full Internet access throughout the territory.
Call for Inclusive Political Dialogue
The UN Human Rights Office said that addressing the underlying grievances of the local population would require meaningful engagement among stakeholders and political representatives.
The High Commissioner calls for meaningful and inclusive political dialogue to address the underlying issues and grievances of the local population.
Official Sources
OHCHR Press Briefing Note: https://www.ohchr.org/en/press-briefing-notes/2026/07/wave-unrest-pakistan-administered-kashmir
UN Video Briefing and Media Assets: https://media.un.org/unifeed/en/asset/d360/d3609420

The statement represents a significant intervention by the UN Human Rights Office ahead of the July 27 Legislative Assembly elections and places international attention on developments in Pakistan-administered Azad Kashmir.
